units.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for .NET reads and writes PDF documents and converts them to other formats. It supports input formats including HTML, SVG, MD, TXT, and PDF, and outputs to PDF, HTML, SVG, and other formats. It provides capabilities for working with annotations, signatures, security, text, forms, logical structure, and tagged PDF content.

Create a new PDF or open an existing one with Document, then add, delete, reorder, rotate, resize, or copy pages across documents through Page and PageCollection; full round-trip save and incremental save preserve bookmarks and outlines, page labels, named destinations, document info, XMP metadata, and optional content layers.

Read, fill, and build AcroForm fields—including text, checkbox, radio, choice, button, signature, date, rich text, file-select, and paper-barcode—through Forms, Field, FormFieldBuilder, FormEditor, and FormDataConverter, including field-level flatten and JSON/XFDF form-data import and export.

Extract text with TextAbsorber, TextFragmentAbsorber, ParagraphAbsorber, and TableAbsorber; find and replace across pages—including cross-operator and ligature-aware spans—and build new text with TextBuilder, TextFragment, TextSegment, TextStamp, and FormattedText, with Bidi (RTL) support and AGL Unicode mapping.

Render pages to PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, or SVG with PngDevice, JpegDevice, BmpDevice, TiffDevice, ThumbnailDevice, and SvgDevice through the pluggable IPageRenderer, with every text rendering mode including stroked and clipped text, luminosity soft masks, axial gradients with any number of colour stops, mesh shading types 4-7, JBIG2 decoding and lossless encoding, and JPEG, JPEG2000, and CCITT-Fax filters.

Encrypt and decrypt with RC4-40, RC4-128, AES-128, and AES-256, and sign documents with PKCS#1 and PKCS#7 / CMS detached signatures—including DocMDP certifying signatures, RFC 3161 document timestamps, and external signing through an ExternalSignature or a SignHash callback—through Security, Signatures, PdfFileSecurity, PdfFileSignature, PdfSigner, and PdfCertificate.

Read an existing StructTreeRoot tree and walk its LogicalStructure element hierarchy, or build tagged content from scratch with Tagged's typed structure elements—including ruby and warichu inline elements and the StructureTypeStandard role set—setting document language, title, alternate text, and marked content for accessibility.

Add and edit every standard annotation type—including link, text, free-text, highlight, square/circle/line/polyline, ink, stamp, popup, file attachment, screen, redaction, watermark, pre-press marks, and rich media—with appearance generation and flatten, and apply redactions to remove glyphs, path segments, image pixels, and associated annotations permanently.

Convert PDF to and from HTML and SVG, load Markdown, XML, plain-text, PostScript, or Encapsulated PostScript files, and export to Markdown, plain text, PDF/A (1A through 4F), or PDF/UA-1, using HtmlLoadOptions, SvgSaveOptions, MdLoadOptions, and TxtLoadOptions.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for .NET provides the Document class as its primary entry point, which exposes pages through Document.Pages (a PageCollection of Page objects), forms through Document.Form, and security features through PdfSigner and PdfCertificate. The API surface includes modules for text extraction, form handling, annotations, security, rendering, logical structure, comparison, format conversion, and loading options.

The Document class serves as the main entry point for working with PDF documents, providing access to pages through Document.Pages (a PageCollection of Page objects), forms through Document.Form, and security features through PdfSigner and PdfCertificate.
Text extraction and manipulation is supported through the TextAbsorber and TextFragmentAbsorber classes, which can visit pages or entire documents to extract text content.
Interactive form handling is provided through the Forms module, which includes Field and ChoiceField classes for accessing and manipulating form fields.
Annotations such as link annotations and stamp annotations are managed through the Annotations module, which includes LinkAnnotation and StampAnnotation classes.
Security features including PDF signing and certificate management are available through the Security module, which includes PdfSigner and PdfCertificate classes.
Rendering pages to images and vector formats is supported through the Devices module, which includes PngDevice and SvgDevice classes.
Logical structure and tagged PDF support is provided through the LogicalStructure module, which includes AutoTaggingSettings and Tagged classes.
PDF comparison functionality is available through the Comparison module, which includes ComparisonMode and GraphicalPdfComparer types.
Format conversion and saving options are provided through the SaveFormat and PdfFormat types, which support various output formats and conversion options.
Loading options for HTML, Markdown, and SVG input are available through HtmlLoadOptions, MdLoadOptions, and SvgSaveOptions classes.
